question: The value of resistance gets doubled if its length is ________ (keeping other parameters constant).
solution:
The correct answer is **__doubled__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance is inversely correlated with wire cross-sectional area and directly correlated with wire length.**
 
• The** resistance doubles if the length of a wire is increased by adding more wire**, while the **cross-sectional area remains unchanged.**
 
• Resistance (R)= ρL/A ​ 
 
• We know that 
 
 
• R=ρL/A ----(i)
 
• If the wire's length doubles, a new resistance will result.
 
• R'= ρ2L/A ------(ii)
 
• By adjusting equation (ii), we obtain
 
• R'= 2R
 
• **Therefore, it follows that the new resistance will similarly double as the wire's length increases.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance**

 
 
• **The ability of an electric conductor to resist the flow of current through it is known as the conductor's resistance.**
 
• R serves as **a symbol** for it.
 
• **Ohm (Ω) is the SI unit for resistance.**
 
• Resistance (R)= ρL/A
 
• Where l is the conductor's length, A is its cross-sectional area, and ρ is the conductor's resistivity?
